articles.title: Handheld Gaming PC or Switch 2: Which Fits How You Play?
articles.excerpt: A handheld PC like the Steam Deck plays your PC game library. A Switch 2 plays Nintendo's games. How to choose based on the games you want and how much setup you will accept.
articles.hero_image_alt: Comparison table of a handheld gaming PC and the Switch 2

body.text: **Choose by the games you want.** A handheld gaming PC such as the Steam Deck plays PC games you buy on stores like Steam. A Switch 2 plays Nintendo's games, which are not sold on PC.
The short comparison

rows: With a dock, bought separately on many models

body.text: What a handheld gaming PC is good at

items: **A huge library.** If you already own PC games, many of them come with you.
**Sales.** PC stores discount games often.
**Flexibility.** You can change graphics settings to trade picture quality for battery life.

body.text: On the Steam Deck, games carry a **Deck Verified** rating that tells you how well each one works on the device. Check it before buying a game for handheld play.
What the Switch 2 is good at

items: **Nintendo's own series,** which you cannot play anywhere else.
**Simplicity.** Every game is made for the hardware, so there are no settings to tune.
**Local multiplayer.** The detachable controllers make it easy to share.

body.text: Things to check before buying a handheld PC

items: **Demanding new games may run poorly or not at all.** Their requirements are written for desktop graphics cards.
**Windows handhelds** can use more game stores and launchers than the Steam Deck, but need more setup.
**Battery life** drops quickly in demanding games.

body.text: Which to choose

items: **You want Mario, Zelda and Pokémon:** Switch 2.
**You have a Steam library and want to play it away from your desk:** a handheld PC.
**You want one device for a family:** Switch 2 is the easier choice.
**You like adjusting settings and trying many kinds of games:** a handheld PC.

body.text: Many players end up with both, because the game libraries barely overlap.
For how the Switch 2 differs from the original, read [Switch 2 vs Switch](/nintendo/switch-2-vs-switch).

articles.title: Xbox Series X vs Series S: Which One Should You Get?
articles.excerpt: Both Xbox consoles play the same games. The Series X targets 4K and has more storage. The Series S is smaller, cheaper and digital-only. How to choose.
articles.hero_image_alt: Comparison table of Xbox Series S and Series X

body.text: Both consoles play the same Xbox games and work with Game Pass. **The Series X is the more powerful console and targets 4K. The Series S is smaller and cheaper, targets 1440p and has no disc drive.**
The differences
The same games on both
Every Xbox Series game runs on both consoles. On the Series S, games usually run at a lower resolution and sometimes with reduced visual settings.
Storage is the Series S's weak point
New games are large. Gears of War: E-Day is about 120 GB on Xbox, according to Pure Xbox. On a 512 GB Series S, a handful of games like that fills the drive.
You can add space with a Storage Expansion Card. Games made for Series X|S have to run from the internal drive or one of those cards, not from an ordinary USB drive.
No disc drive on the Series S
The Series S is digital-only. You buy games from the store or play them through Game Pass. If you own Xbox games on disc, or like buying used games, that points to the Series X with a disc drive.
Choose the Series S if

items: You want the cheapest way into current Xbox games and Game Pass.
You have a 1080p or 1440p screen.
You are happy with digital games and will manage storage.

body.text: Choose the Series X if

items: You have a 4K TV.
You want more storage from the start.
You want to play discs.

body.text: Game Pass works on both

Both consoles use the same Game Pass tiers. For an example of how the tiers differ for a new release, see [which Game Pass tier includes Gears of War: E-Day](/xbox/gears-of-war-e-day-game-pass-tiers).

articles.title: Nintendo Switch 2 vs Switch: What Changed and Is It Worth Upgrading?
articles.excerpt: The Switch 2 has a larger 1080p screen, 4K output when docked, 256 GB of storage and plays most original Switch games. What changed and who should upgrade.
articles.hero_image_alt: Comparison table of the Switch and Switch 2

body.text: The Switch 2 keeps the same idea as the original: one console you play handheld or on a TV. **It has a bigger, sharper screen, much more power, 256 GB of storage and plays most original Switch games.**
The differences

rows: 6.2 inch, 720p (7 inch on the OLED model)
32 GB (64 GB on the OLED model)

body.text: What is new

items: **A bigger, sharper screen** that can refresh up to 120 times a second.
**4K output** when docked to a TV.
**Joy-Con 2 controllers** that attach with magnets and can be used like a mouse in supported games.
**GameChat**, a built-in voice and video chat feature.

body.text: Your old games
The Switch 2 plays most original Switch games, both cartridges and downloads. Some have paid or free upgrades that improve them on the new console.
The memory card catch
Switch 2 games can only be stored on **microSD Express** cards. Standard microSD cards from your old Switch will not work for Switch 2 games, so budget for a new card if 256 GB is not enough.
Worth upgrading?

items: **Yes, if you want the new games.** More and more big releases are Switch 2 only. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 arrives on Switch 2 on October 23, and a Switch 2 version of Minecraft follows on October 27.
**Yes, if you play on a 4K TV** and want a sharper picture.
**Maybe not yet, if you mostly play older Switch games.** They still work on the console you have.

body.text: The Switch 2 launched on June 5, 2025 at $449.99 in the US. Check current prices and bundles before buying.
For this month's releases on every console, see the [October 2026 console release calendar](/releases/october-2026-console-game-releases).

articles.title: PS5 vs PS5 Pro: What the Pro Changes and Who It Is For
articles.excerpt: The PS5 Pro has a faster graphics chip, Sony's PSSR upscaling and 2 TB of storage, but no disc drive in the box. What actually changes and who should buy it.
articles.hero_image_alt: Comparison table of the PS5 and PS5 Pro

body.text: The PS5 Pro plays the same games as the standard PS5. What it adds is **a faster graphics chip, an upscaling feature called PSSR and a 2 TB drive**. It does not come with a disc drive.
The differences

rows: Included or digital-only, depending on model

body.text: What the Pro actually improves
Many PS5 games make you choose between a sharper picture and a smoother frame rate. The Pro is built to give you more of both at once in games that support it.
Sony said at launch that the Pro's graphics chip renders about 45% faster than the standard console's. Games updated for it carry a **PS5 Pro Enhanced** label on the store.
A game without that label still runs on the Pro, but it may look and play the same as on a standard PS5.
What it does not change

items: **There are no Pro-only games.** Everything runs on both consoles.
**Loading is not meaningfully faster.** Both use a fast SSD.
**Your controller, saves and library are the same.**

body.text: The disc drive catch
The Pro has no disc drive in the box. If you own games or films on disc, you need to buy the detachable drive separately. Add that to the cost before comparing prices.
Who should buy the Pro

items: **You have a 4K TV and care about picture quality.** This is who it was made for.
**You play the newest big-budget games** and want the best version on console.

body.text: Who should keep the standard PS5

items: **You have a 1080p TV.** You will see far less of the benefit.
**You mostly play older or less demanding games.**
**Price matters.** The Pro launched at $699.99 in the US in November 2024, well above the standard console. Check current prices before deciding.

body.text: Phantom Blade Zero is one upcoming game with confirmed PS5 Pro enhancements, though its developer has not yet said what they are. See [which October 2026 games are not on your console](/releases/october-2026-console-exclusives).

articles.title: Gears of War: E-Day on Game Pass: Which Tier Do You Need?
articles.excerpt: Gears of War: E-Day is on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass from October 6. Premium gets it later and Essential does not include it. Early access costs extra.
articles.hero_image_alt: Gears of War: E-Day official screenshot

body.text: **Gears of War: E-Day is included with Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass from its launch day, October 6, 2026.** It is not included with Game Pass Essential, and Game Pass Premium members have to wait.
Which tier includes it

rows: Not at launch. Expected later, reported as around October 2027

body.text: This breakdown comes from Pure Xbox's launch guide.
Game Pass does not include early access
Early access began on October 1 for owners of the Premium Edition or Collector's Edition. A Game Pass subscription alone does not unlock it.
If you subscribe and want to start early, you can buy the **Premium Upgrade**, which adds early access and the Premium Edition's bonus content to the Game Pass version.
Where you can play it

items: **Xbox Series X|S:** yes
**PC:** yes, through the Xbox app and Steam
**Xbox One:** through cloud gaming only
**PS5 and Switch 2:** no version announced

body.text: Digital copies support **Xbox Play Anywhere**, so buying it once covers both Xbox and PC.
How much space you need
Pure Xbox lists the install at about 120.5 GB on Xbox Series X|S. Check your free space before launch day, because that is a large share of a Series S drive.
Should you subscribe or buy?

items: **You already have Ultimate or PC Game Pass:** you can play on October 6 at no extra cost.
**You have Premium or Essential:** you would need to upgrade your tier or buy the game.
**You only want this one game and will keep playing for months:** compare the price of the game with the cost of the months you would subscribe.

articles.title: Which October 2026 Games Are Not on Your Console?
articles.excerpt: Gears of War: E-Day skips PS5. Phantom Blade Zero skips Xbox. Enshrouded reaches Xbox months late. Here is what each console misses in October 2026.

body.text: Most of October 2026's big games are on both PS5 and Xbox, but four are not. **Gears of War: E-Day is on Xbox and PC only. Phantom Blade Zero is on PS5 and PC only.**
The games that skip a console
Gears of War: E-Day
The Gears prequel launches on October 6 on Xbox Series X|S and PC. No PS5 or Switch 2 version has been announced. Xbox One owners can play through cloud gaming only.
Phantom Blade Zero

S-GAME's action game launches on October 29 on PS5 and PC. No Xbox version has been announced. Wccftech has reported a 12-month console exclusivity window for PS5, which the studio has not detailed publicly, so treat that as reported and not confirmed.
Enshrouded 1.0
The survival game leaves early access on October 15 on PC and PS5. The Xbox version has been pushed to spring 2027, with no exact date.
Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2
Boltgun 2 arrives on October 14 on PS5, Xbox Series X|S and PC. The Switch 2 version is confirmed but comes "shortly after" the others, according to the announcement.
What this means if you are choosing a console
One month of releases is not a reason to buy a console. Exclusives change from month to month. Look at the series you care about most over a year or more, and which console your friends play on.
For every release this month by date and console, see the [October 2026 console release calendar](/releases/october-2026-console-game-releases).

articles.title: Buying a PS5 SSD? Check the Interface, Heatsink and Fit First
articles.excerpt: Capacity is only one part of a PS5 storage upgrade. Use Sony’s specifications and the exact drive’s dimensions before ordering.
articles.hero_image_alt: Sony official illustration showing the PS5 M.2 SSD installation slot
articles.hero_image_caption: Image: Sony Interactive Entertainment / PlayStation Support

body.text: Two drives can both say M.2 on the box and serve different purposes. For PS5 expansion, match Sony’s supported interface and form factor before comparing capacity or headline speed. A low price is not useful if the drive cannot work in the expansion slot.
Check the exact product listing

rows: PCIe Gen4 x4 M.2 NVMe, Key M
A suitable heatsink or other supported heat-dissipation structure
The drive and cooling assembly meet Sony’s size limits
Sony’s listed range is 250 GB to 8 TB

body.text: Keep the manufacturer’s model number with your shopping notes. Listings can combine several capacities or a bare drive and a heatsink version under one product page. Verify the dimensions of the version you are actually buying, including any attached cooling structure.
Make a storage plan before adding capacity

Look at the games you regularly use, the free space already available and how often you reinstall old favourites. Choose capacity around that routine. Keep budget for the complete compatible assembly rather than assuming a bare SSD is ready for the console.
Follow the instructions for your console model

Sony provides different cover-removal instructions for different PS5 model groups. Use the guide for the number on your console. Update system software and follow the official shutdown and installation procedure. This article is a shopping checklist; it does not replace Sony’s illustrated installation guide.
After installation

items: Expect the console to request formatting when the drive is first used.
Do not use a drive containing your only copy of important data.
Choose where new games install and move one familiar game as an initial test.
Keep the receipt and exact model details in case you need product support.

body.text: A compatible expansion drive adds room for your library. It does not make every game load or perform identically to another drive, and a faster number on the box is not a guaranteed gameplay improvement.

Sony: supported SSD specifications and model-specific installation

articles.title: Steam Deck Verified, Playable or Unknown: What to Check Before Buying
articles.excerpt: Read the compatibility details, then judge controls, text size and your own games instead of treating a badge as a performance score.
articles.hero_image_alt: Steam Deck Verified, Playable or Unknown: What to Check Before Buying — official Valve artwork

body.text: Start with the games you intend to play. A handheld can fit your routine beautifully and still be the wrong purchase if your essential title is unsupported or uncomfortable to use on a small display. Valve’s compatibility labels make a useful first filter, but the details matter more than the colour of the badge.
Read the four labels accurately

rows: Valve reports an experience that works out of the box
Read the setup or usability notes before deciding
Valve has not completed a compatibility review

body.text: Valve’s checks cover input, display, launcher behaviour and system support. That gives you useful information about the practical experience, including whether you need the touchscreen or an on-screen keyboard. It does not guarantee your preferred graphics preset, battery life or performance in every scene.
Build a short personal compatibility list

items: Write down your five most important games rather than a general wish list.
Open each game’s current store compatibility details.
Read the notes for Playable games and decide whether the extra step suits you.
Check the publisher’s launcher, account and online requirements.

body.text: Think about the session, not only the specification

A game with dense menus and small text might suit a desk and larger display even when it launches successfully on a handheld. Conversely, a controller-friendly game you play in short sessions may be a better portable choice than the most demanding title in your library. Judge the device around the sessions you actually want to create.
Recheck after significant updates

Game and system updates can change compatibility. Treat an old video or forum post as a dated experience, then compare it with current store notes and the publisher’s support information. If offline play matters to you, test that requirement independently rather than assuming a compatibility badge promises it.
